findings.F1: The Calmar fails because of one long bear stretch: the book's deepest fall is −61 % (yearly return +30 %), lasting 271 days across w1, w2 and w3 (all 2022), where the book's daily returns summed to −85 % against −74 % for holding the coins, with a correlation of 0.77 to holding.
findings.F2: Every coin lost in that fall, and the book lost more than holding on four of six: BTC −22 % against −15 % for holding, ETH −21 % against −14 %, XMR −6 % against −2 %, LTC −14 % against −14 %, with XRP (−9 % against −12 %) and ZEC (−14 % against −15 %) the exceptions.
findings.F3: The idea's cases split by window. In the five losing windows (w1, w2, w3, w5, w9) the mean unusual 6-day move is −2.27 % (t −4.27, 304 cases). In the other windows it is +1.17 % (t 3.24, 1337 cases).
findings.F4: Being long a 7-day rise does not keep the book out of bear stretches. The book is long on 58 % of bars in the losing windows against 63 % elsewhere. There, the long bars' gain per bar is negative at almost every level of the 30-day return, 7-day return and distance from the 30-day high, for example −0.00084 per bar within 5 % of the 30-day high.
findings.F5: The coin's 60-day return is positive in only 42 % of the cases in the losing windows, against 62 % elsewhere. Among the cases, a 60-day return between −10 % and 0 is followed by −2.2 % (t −2.70, 92 cases), and 0 to +20 % by +1.6 % (t 1.93, 182 cases).
findings.F6: The coin's 15-day return grades the cases. Cases with a 15-day return above 15 % gain +1.8 % unusual (t 2.10, 410 cases), while cases with 0 to 5 % lose −1.3 % (t −2.22, 239 cases).
findings.F7: The break's size grades the trades steeply: from the smallest to the largest fifth of breaks (median 0.10 to 1.54 average 4-hour ranges), the mean net trade result is +1.6, +1.2, +1.8, +4.4 and +8.1 %. Yet the worst tenth of trades loses about 8 to 10 % in every fifth.
findings.F8: Contrary to the brief, breaks out of expanded ranges pay more than breaks out of quiet ones. When the 7-day mean range is above 1.2 times the 30-day one, trades average +6.7 % against +1.4 to +3.4 % below it, and long bars earn +0.00114 per bar in the paying windows against 0.00012 to 0.00061.
findings.F9: The trades are a few large wins over many small losses: 2607 trades held about 8 days, with a median of −0.31 %, a mean of +3.4 % and 43 % winners. The worst 5 % lose 14 % or more and the single worst lose 46 to 56 % on ETH, LTC, XRP and ZEC.
findings.F10: The size is not what fails. The total move per case (+1.30 %) is 6.8 times a 0.19 % round trip and the unusual move 2.6 times. The failure is the depth of the falls, not the gain per trade.

ideas.idea: When a four-hour bar closes above the highest high of a coin's preceding two days, only while the coin's 7-day return is positive and its 60-day return is positive, the coin rises over the next six days. The farther that close sits above the two-day high, measured in the coin's 30-day average four-hour range, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would refuse upward breaks made while the coin is still below its level of two months ago, which is where the cases concentrate in the bear stretches that carry the book's deepest fall.
ideas.name: breakout above rising two months

ideas.idea: When a four-hour bar closes above the highest high of a coin's preceding two days, only while the coin's 7-day return is positive, the coin rises over the next six days. The larger the coin's 15-day return, and the farther that close sits above the two-day high in the coin's 30-day average four-hour range, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would put most weight on large breaks inside a strong half-month rise and little on breaks after a flat two weeks, which lose on average.
ideas.name: breakout graded by fortnight trend

ideas.idea: When a four-hour bar closes above the highest high of a coin's preceding two days while the coin's 7-day average four-hour range is wide against its 30-day average range, the coin rises over the next six days. The wider that recent range against the 30-day one, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would favour breaks that come out of expanding, active markets rather than quiet ones, the reverse of the brief's quiet-range story.
ideas.name: breakout from expanding ranges
